edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with type 2 diabetes or chronic kidney disease
edges.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors restore tubuloglomerular feedback, reduce intraglomerular hypertension, and promote natriuresis, which is why renal protection often appears even before large changes in HbA1c.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Javier meta analysis in Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev already points to sglt2 inhibitors tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.

evidence.citation: JavierRM et al 2026 Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev
